% hypcap's all option with hyperref alone, in figure, figure*, table, and
% table*: each number, \ref, and \autoref as in the PDF, and each link
% landing in its float. A figure without a caption uses no number, a
% float may hold two captions, and a label may sit inside a caption.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\usepackage[all]{hypcap}
\begin{document}
\begin{figure}[h]\centering\fbox{Bare}\end{figure}
\begin{figure}[h]
  \centering
  \fbox{One}
  \caption{First figure}\label{fig:one}
\end{figure}
\begin{figure*}[h]
  \centering
  \fbox{Wide}
  \caption{Wide figure}\label{fig:wide}
\end{figure*}
\begin{table}[h]
  \centering
  \caption{First table}\label{tab:one}
  \begin{tabular}{c}1\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\begin{table*}[h]
  \centering
  \caption{Wide table}\label{tab:wide}
  \begin{tabular}{c}2\end{tabular}
\end{table*}
\begin{figure}[h]
  \begin{minipage}{.45\linewidth}\caption{Left}\label{fig:l}\end{minipage}
  \begin{minipage}{.45\linewidth}\caption{Right}\label{fig:r}\end{minipage}
\end{figure}
\begin{figure}[h]
  \centering
  \fbox{Inner}
  \caption{Inner label\label{fig:inner}}
\end{figure}

Ref: \ref{fig:one}; \ref{fig:wide}; \ref{tab:one}; \ref{tab:wide}.

Autoref: \autoref{fig:one}; \autoref{fig:wide}; \autoref{tab:one}; \autoref{tab:wide}.

More: \ref{fig:l}; \autoref{fig:inner}.

Second caption: \ref{fig:r}.
\end{document}
